title: NASA gear noise rig: one tooth pair loaded statically, fillet strain at the 30 degree tangent

provenance.geometry: Oswald, Townsend, Rebbechi, Lin, Dynamic Forces in Spur Gears: Measurement, Prediction, and Code Validation, NASA TM-107223 (1996), Table 1: 28/28 teeth, module 3.175 mm (diametral pitch 8), pressure angle 20 deg, face width 6.35 mm; Oswald, Lin, Delgado, DANST PC version 3.00 user manual, NASA TM-107291 (1996), test case 1 (the same rig): cutter edge radius ratio 0.40, tooth clearance 0.25/P (dedendum 1.25 m), outside diameter modelled 3.738 in for a 0.006 in edge break, backlash 0.007 in, linear tip relief 0.0010 in from 24.5 deg roll, E = 30e6 psi, nu = 0.3
provenance.rig: NASA TM-107223: the calibration rig loads a single tooth (the mating gear's other teeth ground away) statically, one gear-shaft assembly on linear bearings so that friction is cancelled; strain gauges 0.38 mm long in the driven gear's root fillets at the 30 degree tangency location, on the loaded (tensile) and unloaded (compressive) sides
provenance.assumed: not stated in the sources, chosen here: the gear blank is solid to a bore of 25.4 mm held rigidly (the gears are press-fitted and keyed, 'thick-rim'); the gauges sit at mid-face; the tip relief of test case 1 on both gears
